title: Amplifier Surge Readiness & Rollback Scenarios
topics: canary sizing and smoke test plan
KV cache warming and eviction strategy
fallback model routing and quantization safety
summary: Pre-launch operational sync focused on planned traffic amplifier (surge) gating, explicit rollback steps, and validation checklist. Decided to run phased 50% smoke test on Monday, produce a simplified one-page rollback playbook, and add two new alerts (cache-eviction and kv-fill-rate). Owner assignments and due dates captured.
next_steps: Lia to publish one-page rollback playbook and send to execs (due 2026-11-11)
Ethan to add KV fill-rate and cache-eviction alerts to Sentry/Prometheus and test (due 2026-11-10)
Marco to validate runtime fallback to smaller quantized model under burst (validate by 2026-11-10)
Priya to rehearse autoscale step-down sequence and document manual override (due 2026-11-11)
Noah to circulate canary traffic runbook and monitoring links before Monday smoke test
action_items: Lia Gomez: finalize rollback runbook and share PDF with execs (due 2026-11-11)
Ethan Cole: implement KV fill-rate alert and run synthetic that triggers it (due 2026-11-10)
Marco Lin: run fallback-to-quantized-model test on staging and share logs (due 2026-11-10)
Priya Kapoor: document and test manual autoscale override steps (due 2026-11-11)
Jenna Brooks: create quick smoke test checklist and verify end-to-end latencies (due 2026-11-10)
Carlos Mendes: confirm spare capacity corridor and confirm node tagging for surge (due 2026-11-10)
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-09 14:00 PST
Duration: ~72 minutes
Attendees: Anika, Ethan, Priya, Marco, Noah, Lia, Samir, Jenna, Carlos

00:00 Anika Rao: okay hey everybody thanks for carving time, I'm gonna kick us off. The agenda is short: surge gating, rollback, canary sizing, and action owners. We'll do a quick risk callout after each item.
00:18 Samir Patel: hey, quick note -- oncall team is flagged for Monday so we want to be explicit about who owns the first 60 minutes.
00:25 Lia Gomez: yes we need a single decision maker. That should be Lia as release owner but Samir will be escalation.
00:33 Anika Rao: perfect, Lia decision maker, Samir escalation. Jenna are you okay to run the smoke checklist?
00:40 Jenna Brooks: yep that's my lane, I'll edit it this afternoon. Quick question: do we have an updated failure threshold for the new quantized model?
00:50 Marco Lin: um, we measured tail latency increase but token cost dropped, for the 4k prompt baseline tail 95 rose by ~60 ms in staging last week. It was acceptable for our SLO but under high KV fill it spiked more.
01:08 Priya Kapoor: that's the thing — if KV cache warms too slowly under surge we saw double hits to the model which drives cost and latency. We need eviction alerts.
01:18 Ethan Cole: agreed. I propose two new alerts: kv_fill_rate > 80% for 5m and cache_evictions/sec > X. If both fire, we scale up or enable prefix-cache bypass?
01:30 Marco Lin: prefix-cache bypass is risky; fallback to a slightly smaller model variant with higher batch efficiency might be safer for latency.
01:39 Samir Patel: but that changes quality, product needs to sign off.
01:43 Anika Rao: noted — we'll include product acceptance in the rollback page. Lia, do you want a decision matrix pinned to the runbook?
01:50 Lia Gomez: yes, a simple matrix: alert -> immediate action -> who, with checkboxes. Keep it one page. Execs want clarity.
02:00 Carlos Mendes: on capacity: we've reserved a spare corridor of nodes but need node tagging so automation targets the right pool during surge. I'll confirm tags today.
02:08 Priya Kapoor: make sure the autoscaler won't pull from other customers in Dedicated pools; show explicit pool IDs.
02:16 Anika Rao: good call. Action: Carlos confirm node tags and share pool IDs.

02:45 Jenna Brooks: can we talk canary sizing? If we do 10% canary for 30m we might not trigger the edge-case kv pressure. 50% for 10 minutes is more likely to stress it. Thoughts?
02:58 Noah Hart: for confidence I'd rather do a phased run: start 10% for 15m, then 50% for 10m if no alerts and manual go. That gives a controlled ramp with explicit abort points.
03:16 Samir Patel: acceptable if we have a manual abort and the oncall is paged.
03:23 Marco Lin: also need to warm the KV before we open the valve. We can run a synthetic prefix-fill job for 20 minutes pre-canary. It must be run from the same region to exercise locality.
03:36 Priya Kapoor: ETA on that job?
03:38 Marco Lin: I can spin it up in staging today, and in prod as a short warm-up 5 minutes before the 10% step. But we need to ensure it doesn't distort analytics. Tag the traffic as 'warmup'.
03:50 Anika Rao: good, put warm-up in the checklist. Jenna take that.
03:55 Jenna Brooks: noted. I'll add warmup steps and tagging.

04:10 Anika Rao: let's discuss rollback automation. We have two axes: automated fallback (if X alerts fire) and manual rollback via release portal. We need both. What are the exact trigger thresholds?
04:23 Ethan Cole: automated fallback should be conservative: if 3 of 4 critical alerts fire within 2 minutes -> trigger fallback to smaller model and route 30% away. Manual rollback needs a single human approve but quick button.
04:33 Lia Gomez: execs won't like automatic product-quality fallback without notice. Can we configure automatic to only adjust to low-impact routes, like non-critical tenants or lower-tier traffic?
04:45 Marco Lin: yes we can route by customer_tier. For hosted API default to route to deduped lower-cost model only for 'best-effort' class. But our corporate traffic will remain pinned until manual.
04:58 Anika Rao: ok so automatic fallback for best-effort, manual for critical and enterprise. Document defaults and exceptions.
05:07 Samir Patel: and logging — every fallback must create an audit event with reason code and a memdump link — so SRE can postmortem.
05:16 Marco Lin: we'll include that: audit events + trace ID. I'll make sure runtime emits the reason.

05:45 Lia Gomez: about the rollback playbook content: one page, matrix, single-decision-maker, contact list, abort steps, known caveats, and where to find logs. Also include 'when not to rollback' guidance (e.g., scheduled DB maintenance).
05:58 Jenna Brooks: I have a list of false positives we saw last quarter — I'll attach as appendix link.
06:05 Anika Rao: put appendix link in Confluence and link it in the one-pager.

06:30 Carlos Mendes: capacity question — we still have a small risk that autoscale fails to add nodes under burst due to quota issues. We should pre-borrow capacity by starting spare nodes in warm pool.
06:44 Priya Kapoor: that costs a bit but is cheaper than a failed launch. Let's quantify cost and present to finance if needed. Carlos, please send us numbers.
06:53 Carlos Mendes: will do.

07:15 Marco Lin: technical deep-dive: quantized model fallback path requires KV transform compatibility — we found one mismatch in tokenization edge where kv keys differed. I'm chalking that up to our tokenizer normalization. We need a small migration job to canonicalize keys or fallback will see cache misses.
07:33 Priya Kapoor: can you estimate the migration run time?
07:36 Marco Lin: dependent on corpus size but in staging it's minutes. In prod might be an hour if not sharded; we'll shard. I'll provide exact estimate by EOD.
07:45 Anika Rao: add that to action items.

08:05 Samir Patel: runbook must also specify who disables the planned traffic if manual rollback is necessary — will it be Lia or Samir?
08:12 Lia Gomez: Lia decides but Samir executes the disable. We'll record that.

08:30 Jenna Brooks: ops checklist: smoke tests, warm-up tagging, latency & error dashboards, kv metrics, model-quality quick checks, and sanity sample checks for hallucination spike.
08:45 Noah Hart: include a sampling hook to pull 50 random requests for human review post-canary. We'll limit PII exposure, redaction needed.
08:55 Priya Kapoor: good reminder on compliance — redact request text before sampling. Add that step.

09:20 Anika Rao: timing — Monday: pre-warm at 09:40, 10:00 start 10% for 15m, assess, then manual decision to move to 50% for 10m. If we reach 50% and signals are green, continue ramp per rollout plan. Otherwise rollback. Everyone comfortable?
09:39 Samir Patel: yes, oncall paged for pre-warm and canary.
09:44 Carlos Mendes: spare nodes will be staged by 09:30.
09:48 Lia Gomez: I'll publish the rollback one-pager tonight and ping execs.

10:05 Action recap (Anika): Lia publish playbook; Ethan add KV alerts; Marco validate fallback; Priya document autoscale override; Jenna finalize smoke checklist; Carlos confirm node tags and capacity numbers; Noah circulate runbook links.
10:20 Quick risks: 1) KV mismatch (Marco) 2) Autoscaler quota slip (Carlos) 3) Unexpected quality regression on fallback (Product acceptance).
10:40 Samir Patel: if any of those trigger, abort and rollback. Soundboard agreed.

11:00 Closing: Lia will share the PDF and Confluence link, Ethan will run alert tests, Marco will push runtime audit event change. We'll reconvene if any alerts fire during dry-run. Thanks all.
11:12 Meeting ends.
